title: Token Bank + Latency Horizon Routing (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

Notes for an alternative admission/routing primitive that tries to be more predictable for tail-latency SLAs across regional clusters with heterogeneous GPU pools. This is a working draft — sketches, heuristics, and open questions below. Focus: combining a token-bank concept with a time-window latency horizon and multi-signal control-plane feedback (queue depth, GPU utilization, running inflight tail percentiles).

Problem summary (why this):
- We need a lightweight, global policy that lets the control plane decide: allow, queue, or redirect requests across regions / capacity pools while keeping P95/P99 latency targets and avoiding noisy thrashing between regions.
- Simple token buckets at ingress are too coarse: they don't account for queue depth, variable per-request compute cost, or hot-shard GPU saturation.
- Reactive autoscaling and per-node signals are too slow to prevent SLO violations at the tail.

High-level idea (Token Bank + Latency Horizon):
- Token Bank: instead of per-route token buckets only, maintain a small, soft-state "token bank" per region/pool and per-priority lane. Tokens represent the right to start new requests on that pool. Banks are seeded by the control plane based on predicted throughput capacity and conservative headroom.
- Latency Horizon: for each pool we track a short sliding-window latency horizon (e.g., 30s of tail metrics: P95 and P99 request-start-to-first-token and end-to-end). If the horizon exceeds configured thresholds, the bank drains faster (or becomes frozen) and the control plane attempts routing alternatives.
- Multi-signal gating: token issuance is gated by a weighted synthesis of signals: queue depth (Lq), GPU utilization (u), inflight KV cache pressure (k), and short-term loss/timeout rate (x). The gating function returns a score s in [0,1] used to scale token issuance rate.

Components and responsibilities:
- Edge/ingress: lightweight token reservation client that requests tokens from a local agent (co-located with LB). If no token immediately available, ingress may either queue locally (bounded queue) or proxy/redirect to alternate pool depending on route policy.
- Local agent (per-region): maintains the token bank state, synthesizes signals, and exposes a small API: AcquireToken(priority, estimated_cost) => granted|queue|redirect(reason). Also produces telemetry to control plane (minute-level and 5s-level aggregates).
- Control plane (central/orchestrator): sets bank budgets per pool, computes conservative seeds based on provisioned GPUs, and adjusts seeds using short-term model of request mix and quantization profile. Responsible for multi-region routing decisions when redirect is recommended.

Token semantics and accounting:
- Token = permission to dispatch a request that will allocate N GPU-seconds estimated by the ingress or by an estimator in the agent. We allow fractional tokens (e.g., 0.2 tokens for cheap rerank requests).
- Tokens are time-limited: acquired tokens must be consumed within T_consume (e.g., 5s) or they expire and return to bank (but flagged as expired to avoid gaming).
- Overdrafts: local agent can allow a limited, decaying overdraft to avoid head-of-line blocking for critical requests; overdrafts cost in the bank accounting and are penalized by control-plane reconciliation (throttles or priority changes).

Gating function (canonical form):
- s = clamp( w_q * f_q(Lq) + w_u * f_u(u) + w_k * f_k(k) + w_x * f_x(x), 0, 1 )
- f_q: maps queue depth percentile to 0..1 (exponential after threshold)
- f_u: maps GPU util to 0..1 with knee at 70-80% (soft cap to avoid tail spikes)
- f_k: KV cache pressure / memory pressure mapped aggressively (cache miss bursts can cause big increases in latency)
- f_x: recent timeout/failed requests (1 means system unhealthy)
- Weights are tunable per-pool; default bias towards queue depth and GPU util.

Local queueing behavior (horizon-aware):
- Small local FIFO/NB queue per priority (max depth q_max configurable). When token can't be acquired, the agent decides:
  - Queue locally with adaptive backoff (exponential) if latency horizon within soft target and queue depth below q_warn.
  - Otherwise, immediately request cross-region reroute/redirect.
- Queue admission must enforce per-tenant fairness (soft share buckets) to avoid one tenant filling local queue.

Multi-region routing policy ideas:
- Preferred-first: try local pool if tokens available and horizon healthy. Otherwise, expand to sister-region pools by preference order with a small added network latency budget.
- Gradient routing: route probabilistically to sibling pools where bank health score is highest; control plane maintains a short list of candidate pools and their bank scores.
- Fallback lanes: low-cost/low-quality model variants (quantized/shorter context) can be returned by the local agent if downstream latency is critical and the bank is exhausted. This is an explicit, controlled degradation path.

Control plane reconciliation and seed computation:
- Seed bank budgets are derived from: number_of_gpus * avg_throughput_per_gpu * utilization_headroom_factor * priority_share. Priority_share may be changed dynamically.
- Reconciliation loop every 10s: aggregate per-region telemetry, compute bank adjustments (+/-) and push deltas. Control plane also detects oscillations and applies damping.

Telemetry and metrics to expose (non-exhaustive):
- bank.tokens.total, bank.tokens.available, bank.tokens.overdraft
- gate.score, gate.components: [q_score, u_score, k_score, x_score]
- local_queue.depth, local_queue.wait_time_p50/p95/p99
- gpu.utilization_p50/p95, gpu.saturated_nodes_count
- request.redirects.count and redirect_latency_cost
- degraded_responses.count and fraction_by_tenant

Policy knobs (configurable per-pool):
- q_max, q_warn, overdraft_limit, T_consume, seed_base, headroom_factor, weights for gating function, latency_horizon_window

Operational concerns and mitigations:
- Time sync and stamping: short windows (5s-30s) rely on reasonably synchronized clocks; use monotonic counters where possible.
- Noise & flapping: fast control loops can cause oscillation; put minimal smoothing and a per-pool damping parameter.
- Hot requests: single very heavy requests (long context, expensive ops) must be accounted via estimated_cost. If estimator undercounts, add a runaway detection that marks node as unhealthy and reduces bank seed.
- Security & fairness: tokens represent resource rights — add signed short-lived tokens if cross-region requests may be proxied across tenants or partners. Audit logs for overdraft events.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Local agent prototyping: implement gating function and simple token bank on a canary region, no cross-region routing. Measure p95/p99 improvements vs baseline under synthetic load.
2) Seed control plane: basic seed computation and reconciliation loop, push seeds to canary agent.
3) Probabilistic cross-region routing: add routing decisions and passive telemetry to sibling regions (dry-run).
4) Active redirect + fallback lanes: enable redirects with explicit degraded model variants for critical low-latency paths.
5) Gradual tenant exposure: start with platform internal tenants, then expand to self-serve customers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best estimate per-request GPU-seconds for heterogeneous models? ML-based estimator vs heuristics? (Evan to prototype simple estimator for seq_len/model combo)
- What damping parameters avoid flapping at 5s reconciliation windows? Run stress tests.
- How to handle bursts from identical short requests that still saturate KV caches even at low GPU utilization? Need separate KV-pressure gating.
- Policy UX: how will product expose headroom/priority config to customers without exposing too many knobs?

Action items:
- Evan: build a minimal local-agent simulator that implements the gating function and token bank (due 2025-01-24).
- Zoe: define metrics dashboard (bank health, gate components, redirect counts) and a SLI plan for rollout (due 2025-01-27).
- Arjun: prototype a conservative seed computation formula and synthetic scenarios to validate (due 2025-01-26).

Notes to self: this should be treated as complementary to existing admission work (queue-slope/priority-stack sketches). The unique angle here is explicit resource accounting (token-as-GPU-seconds) + short latency horizon that allows early redirects rather than late reactive shedding. Keep the first prototype simple and focused on observability so we can iterate on weights and thresholds.

References and inspirations: prioritized-bank idea from cloud thin-provisioning papers, admission-control literature with token-bucket variants, our own earlier sketches (see JIRA-PLAT-987).

End of draft.
